subject: Mythology
title: Constellations: Greek Myths in the Sky
description: A fast breakdown of Constellations: Greek Myths in the Sky for builders.

hook.text: When you look at the night sky, nearly half the visible constellations are characters from Greek myths.

buildup.text: Orion the hunter, Andromeda the princess, and Pegasus the winged horse all shine above us every night.

discovery.text: The Greeks placed their heroes in the stars as eternal monuments, turning the sky into a storybook.

twist.text: NASA still uses these mythological names today: Apollo missions, Mercury program, and the Artemis rockets.

climax.text: Greek myths gave humanity a shared map of the sky that navigators, poets, and scientists still use.

punchline.text: We named the stars after gods and then used them to fly.

quiz.question: Which NASA program took its name from Greek mythology?
